findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 1, Harm 4
Raise: Security
Case: normal use - a developer runs the suite with a personal GH_TOKEN in their environment. The shared gh stub writes that real token to gh-tokens.jsonl on every call. Failed test directories are retained by pytest.ini, leaving plaintext copies after the run; the scheduled full suite also supplies a real GitHub token in .github/workflows/forge.yml:217. Isolate the stub from inherited credentials while retaining the dummy-token checks.
Adds work: prevent logging inherited credentials; F 1 x H 3 = 3; 2 x C = 2
findings.title: Keep inherited GitHub credentials out of the test log

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - a shell exports an empty GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN while gh has a stored sign-in and the developer's app is installed. This presence check disables app discovery, so every call silently spends the personal budget. Doctor makes the same presence check at ghapp.py:399 and claims an empty variable supplies the identity. The R33 decision addressed an actual environment credential selecting another account; it did not account for [gh ignoring empty token variables](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cli/go-gh/trunk/pkg/auth/auth.go). If GH_TOKEN is empty and GITHUB_TOKEN is populated, doctor also names the wrong variable.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - an owner installs the app on all organization repositories. Doctor prints the warning but skips token creation and the budget read entirely, so it never shows either remaining hourly budget. It also claims the app will be used without checking whether GitHub will issue its token. The test at tests/test_github_app_token.py:124 explicitly expects only the installation lookup, so it preserves this gap.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - doctor falls back because no app is saved, the installation is pending, or GitHub refuses a token. These cases check identity or repair text but do not assert the displayed personal budget. They also do not verify that the missing-app and pending-install cases add no problem row, while a refused token does add one. Doctor could omit the fallback budget or assign the wrong problem status and this named proof would still pass.
findings.title: Gate: test_1_doctor_shows_who_close_acts_as_and_the_budget_left

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a land train polls checks while its child commands merge, or a developer supplies an explicit credential. The land log combines parent and child calls, but the test requires only any app-token call; child merges would satisfy it even if all parent polling used the personal sign-in. The fallback loop at line 291 also only excludes two fake app tokens, and its log does not record GITHUB_TOKEN. Dropping or replacing the developer's credential would therefore pass because the stub does not authenticate. The proof list claims both land identity and both credential overrides.

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 2, Harm 2
Case: normal use - a developer separates work and personal SSH keys with an origin such as git@github-work:acme/app.git, where SSH config maps github-work to github.com. Git's get-url leaves that hostname in place, so this match rejects it and close, merge and land silently use the personal sign-in; doctor also omits the identity and warning. [GitHub CLI resolves SSH host aliases](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cli/cli/trunk/pkg/cmd/factory/remote_resolver.go); R35 addressed Git insteadOf rules, a different expansion.
Adds work: resolve GitHub SSH aliases; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 4
